historical_references.reference: Jimmy Morrow, a prominent figure in the Indian independence movement, was often referred to as 'Jimmy' by his comrades due to his English nickname. He was born on February 17, 1905, in what is now Bangladesh. Jimmy joined the Indian National Congress in 1927 and was highly influential in organizing protests and civil disobedience campaigns in Bengal. He was also instrumental in the Quit India Movement of 1942. Jimmy was arrested multiple times for his activities and spent several years in prison. He died on December 15, 1955.

Jaswant Singh Rai, popularly known as Jimmy, was a Sikh military officer who served in the British Indian Army during World War I. He was born in 1887 in Punjab, India. Jimmy was awarded the Victoria Cross, the highest military decoration, for his bravery during the Battle of Arras in France in 1917. He was later promoted to the rank of Major. Jimmy continued to serve in the army until his retirement in 1922.
